column2: Abimelech son of Jerubbaal addresses his maternal brothers and all his mother's household kin at Shechem; the maternal network remains explicit.
The comparison is seventy ruling sons versus one lord, followed by flesh and bone kinship; the selected flesh-before-bone order remains.
The maternal brothers repeat all his words to all Shechem's men, whose heart inclines because he is their brother; the kinship rationale remains.
Seventy silver pieces from Baal of the Covenant's house hire empty and startled followers; no shekel unit or familiar reckless-men description is substituted.
column3: Empty and startled exposes the selected kenous/thamboumenous; their contextual social sense remains a lexical question.

column2: Abimelech kills the stated seventy brothers at Ephrathah upon one stone, while youngest Jotham survives by hiding; the printed seventy is retained despite the survivor notice.
Shechem's men and Maallon's whole house make Abimelech king by the oak of the standing-place; selected Maallon and the tree/site expression remain.
column3: Standing-place for stasis and the precise landmark need geographical/lexical assessment; no pillar identification is imposed.

column2: Jotham stands on Gerizim, raises his voice and calls for Shechem's hearing, with an optative wish that God hear them; may preserves that mood.
The trees go to anoint a king for themselves and address the olive; the fable's king-making purpose and first invitation remain.
The olive's richness is what God and humans glorified in it, followed by the question about abandoning it to rule; the selected direction of honor is retained.
The trees' invitation to the fig keeps both Come and reign over us, matching the repeated fable pattern.
The fig's sweetness and good produce are both weighed against ruling the trees; neither productive gift is omitted.
The vine receives the same Come/reign invitation, preserving the sequence after olive and fig.
Wine is human gladness from God, followed by the repeated question about ruling; the selected construction is not rewritten as wine gladdening God.
The bramble is addressed with explicit you, retaining the personal emphasis in You come and reign.
Truthful anointing leads to trust in the bramble's shelter; otherwise fire is wished against Lebanon's cedars. Both condition and optative threat remain.
Truth, integrity, good treatment of Jerubbaal's house and recompense of his hand begin the long condition before the parenthetic account.
column3: The final if is shared by English coordination rather than repeated; the condition remains in scope through did to him.

column2: The father fought for them, cast his life into danger and rescued them from Midian; danger interprets the adversarial throwing-forth image without adding a separate battle event.

Today's revolt, seventy sons on one stone and kingship for the slave girl's son because of kinship remain; the accusation's slave-girl description is not harmonized to the narrator's concubine wording in 8:31.
The condition is resumed after the parenthesis, with wishes for blessing and mutual joy between the people and Abimelech; the selected blessing clause remains.
Both if-not clauses and both directions of consuming fire remain, naming Shechem and Maallon's house each time; the second condition is not deleted as redundant.
Jotham runs, travels and flees to selected Rara, remaining because of brother Abimelech; Rara is not replaced with Beer.
Abimelech's rule over Israel lasts three years; the scope is Israel, not only Shechem.
God sends an evil spirit between the parties, and Shechem acts faithlessly toward Abimelech's house; agency and the household object remain.
column3: Spirit's narrative function is retained without imposing a psychological or demonic explanation beyond the selected wording.

column2: The purpose brings the brothers' wrong and blood onto Abimelech and the men who strengthened his hands; wrong against the sons interprets the genitive as the injustice they suffered.
Mountaintop ambush and plunder of road travelers lead to a report to Abimelech; the unnamed informant is not supplied.
Gaal son of Abed and his brothers enter Shechem, whose men trust him; the selected patronymic remains.
Harvesting, treading, dances, entering the god's house, eating, drinking and cursing form the full sequence; grapes is the contextual object supplied to treading.
Gaal's what/who questions, son of Shechem, Jerubbaal's son, Zebul's overseer/slave descriptions and Hamor's men remain in the difficult selected structure.
column3: The his pronouns, attachment of slave and the identity of son of Shechem are unresolved; no familiar imperative serve Hamor's men is imported.

column2: The wish for control of this people precedes future removal of Abimelech and a future challenge to enlarge his force; the speech is not presented as an already delivered message.
Zebul is the city's ruler and becomes furious on hearing Gaal's words; both office and reaction remain.
The messengers carry gifts, and Behold introduces the arrival and siege accusation; gifts is selected, not a secretly paraphrase.
The instruction is a night rising and field ambush with the accompanying people; time and location remain.
Sunrise, early advance, Behold the coming opponents and doing what the hand finds remain; possible gives idiomatic English to the hand's opportunity.
Abimelech and all accompanying people prepare the night ambush in four companies; four is not harmonized with the later three-company operation.
Morning and Gaal's gate position precede Abimelech's rising from ambushes; the timing and plural ambushes remain.
Gaal's Behold report of descending people is countered by Zebul's mountain-shadow claim; the image and dispute remain.
Gaal speaks again with Behold, a sea-directed descent by the Navel of the Land and one company by the Watchers' Oak; all selected geographical expressions remain.
column3: Navel and watchers are working translated landmark expressions, not independently established geographic identifications.

column2: Zebul challenges Gaal's earlier mouth/boast, points with Behold to the despised people and commands battle; the repeated Abimelech question remains in the quotation.
Gaal goes out from before Shechem's men to fight Abimelech; the selected relation is not changed to an explicit leadership title.
Abimelech pursues, Gaal flees, and many fall as far as the city's entrances; the endpoints and distinct agents remain.
column3: Inherited slain interprets traumatiai in the battle context; wounded is a possible broader rendering requiring lexical review. The retention does not establish that every casualty died.

column2: Abimelech stays at Arima while Zebul expels Gaal's family from Shechem; the negative residence purpose remains.
The next-day movement is into the plain, and Abimelech receives another report; the selected plain is not silently changed to the preceding field term.

The three-company division and ambush remain. Restore the explicit discovery marker with He looked, and behold, the people came out of the city, then separate his rising and striking into the next sentence.
Abimelech and accompanying companies take the gate, while two companies pour over the field people; final singular he struck them remains despite preceding plural groups.
Abimelech fights all day; plural they capture, then singular he kills, demolishes and sows salt. The agency shifts and salt action remain.
All Shechem Tower's men enter Baal of the Covenant's stronghold; the tower group and religious-house refuge remain distinct descriptions.
The gathering of all the tower men is reported to Abimelech; no new actor or tactical inference is inserted.
Abimelech and all his people ascend Zalmon; he takes an axe, cuts a wood load, lifts it to his shoulders and commands quick imitation, preserving the complete model action.
Each cuts and carries a load, follows and places it at the stronghold, then burns it over the occupants. About a thousand men and women die; the approximate total includes both.
Abimelech goes to Thebez, besieges and captures it; the later surviving tower is not treated as a contradiction to be rewritten.
All men, women and leaders flee into the city's fortified tower, shut themselves in and climb to its roof; the distinct leadership group remains.
The defenders fight Abimelech as he approaches the tower, and he nears its door to burn it; plural defenders are not replaced with Abimelech as the fighting subject.
A woman throws a millstone fragment on Abimelech and crushes his skull; the selected fragment is not expanded into a whole upper millstone.

The urgent armour-bearer request preserves the feared report that a woman killed him. Restore the explicit final Abimelech died instead of he died, making clear that the death subject is not the preceding young man.
Israel sees Abimelech's death and disperses each to his own place; the distributive return remains.
God returns Abimelech's wickedness toward his father in killing seventy brothers; the source's stated seventy and paternal relation remain.
God returns all Shechem's wickedness upon their heads, and Jotham son of Jerubbaal's curse reaches them; the concluding twofold repayment remains.
